label: Huawei NetEngine 8000 F8 (6.4T bundle: 4x 8x100GE + 4x 72x10GE)
description: NetEngine 8000 F8 13U router quoted in Huawei's 6.4T bundle: 32x 100GE/50GE/40GE QSFP28 in LPU slots 1-4 (8 per CR8DE8NB00F0) and 288x 10GE/GE SFP+ in slots 5-8 (72 per CR8DERXFMSF0) - 6.08 Tbit/s of port capacity inside a 28.86 Tbit/s switch fabric, 2362 W typical. Eight LPU slots, 1:1 SRU and MPU redundancy, no PoE anywhere.
notes:
Huawei figures for the NetEngine 8000 F8 (chassis CR8PBKPF8DC0). Sources: hardware guide "NetEngine 8000 F8, 8000E F8 V800R024C10SPC500 / Issue 06 (2026-06-30)" EDOC1100280456 (https://support.huawei.com/enterprise/en/doc/EDOC1100280456 - readable only to a crawler user agent, a desktop UA gets HTTP 403); the F8 datasheet PDF (https://e.huawei.com/marketingcloud/pep/asset/20000001/Material/e679822234f94651b2c2153c21a6621b/M2T1A669N893162565584830493/NetEngine%208000%20F8%20Universal%20Service%20Router%20Datasheet.pdf); the series page (https://e.huawei.com/en/products/routers/ne8000).

Chassis, from guide Table 3-2 and Table 3-3: 12 slots - LPU slots 1-8, SRU slots 9-10 (1:1), MPU slots 11-12 (1:1), PM slots PWR1-PWR6, fans FAN1-FAN3; number of service board slots 8; 578.5 mm (13U) x 442 x 482.8 mm; 121.6 kg in the full 6.4T bundle; switching capacity 11.35 Tbit/s in the 1.6T/2T bundles and 28.86 Tbit/s in the 6.4T bundle. The 2022 datasheet edition quotes the older bundle only - 1680 W typical, 2 Tbps forwarding, "up to 32 PICs, 8 LPUCs" per chassis and a device maximum of "24 x 100GE; 240 x 10GE; 320 x GE; 512 x E1; 256 x STM" - which is the PIC-based 1.6T/2T build, not this one.

The board complement is Huawei's own, not a guess: the guide quotes typical power for the 6.4T bundle as "2362 W (configured with SRU 6T4-B and four 8x100GE ports and four 72x10GE ports)", and that is the configuration modelled here. CR8DE8NB00F0 (LPUC-800-CM, 03050LDQ) is 8x QSFP28 100GE/50GE/40GE, ports 0-7, no MACsec, 40/50/100GE auto-sensing, with ports [0,2], [1,3], [4,6] and [5,7] switching Ethernet/breakout mode together and breakout to 1x50GE/1x40GE on an SRU-6T4-A or 4x25GE/4x10GE on an SRU-6T4-B. CR8DERXFMSF0 (LPUC-800-CM) is 72x 10GE/GE (SFP+/SFP optical modules) with MACsec, no breakout, GE/10GE auto-sensing, and LAN/WAN mode switchable only in sub-groups of four or three ports ({4,4,4,3} x4 + {4,4,4}).

Which slots hold which board is this entry's own choice, and the only invented thing in it: the guide states the mix, not the placement. It is safe to re-arrange - every LPUC-800-CM board is installable in any of LPU slots 1-8 when the chassis carries an SRU-6T4-B, and the FlexE slot limits (slots 3/6, or 4/5, on an SRU-6T4-A) bind only the FlexE feature, not the ports.

Licence caveat worth knowing before cabling: on both board types the high-speed mode is rate-limited to 100 Mbit/s until the RTU licence is loaded - the 8x100GE ports are limited by default and only the RTU licence unlocks 40/50/100GE, and the 72-port board is unlimited in GE mode but limited to 100 Mbit/s in 10GE mode.

Not modelled: the MGMT RJ45, console and TOD/CLK ports on the MPUs (out-of-band, like the F1A entry); the PIC-based builds (LPUT-800-CM CR8DLPUTK0C0 plus up to four PICs per slot - 10x 10GE/GE SFP+, 10x 100/1000Base-X SFP, 8x 100/1000Base-RJ45, 4x 10GE SFP+, 2x50G/1x100G QSFP28, 16x E1, 4x channelized STM-1c POS, 8x STM-1c/STM-4c POS); CR8DERGF00F1 (LPUC-100, 72x 100/1000Base-X SFP GE); CR8DEKNBXFF0 (4x 100GE + 40x 10GE/GE); CR8DE1KB00F0 (1x 400G QSFP-DD); the VSUP-100 service card. Each is a different box and needs its own entry.

Capabilities: MPLS, SRv6, EVPN, FlexE, 1588v2 and BGP are software features of the platform, and BGP/OSPF run here off l3-forward; "mpls" and "bgp" are not capability tokens the engine implements, so declaring them would only produce an ignored-token warning. No PoE on any board, at any rate.
